pat: quick note: onboarding canary for titan-int4 shows a parse spike on streaming funcalls when prompts include small code blocks. sharing short repro + plan.

kevin: numbers?

pat: baseline fp16/int8 ~0.1%, int4 jumped to 1.4% on the same 3k test set. failures concentrated on templates with ``` fenced code or markdown tables.

neha: can you paste a reassembled stream that failed?

pat: here's one exact reassembly (chunks in order):

[chunk0] "{\n  \"action\": \"apply_patch\",\n  \"args\": {\n    \"patch\": \"diff --git a/foo b/foo\n+print(1)\"\n"
[chunk1] "\n  }\n}\n"
[chunk2] "FOOTER:trace=aa33\n\n"

pat: chunk1 ends before array/object closure occasionally because int4 emits EOS earlier; footer arrives and sometimes interleaves, producing truncation or stray footer mid-json.

kevin: sounds like the same async-logging flush race we saw in the other canaries. ops-bot: linked PR 1920 in logging-adapter that changed flush timing.

ops-bot: PR 1920 flagged; revert candidate open (LOG-935).

neha: short-term mitigation: sanitizer that strips known footers (FOOTER:, TRACE:, BUILD-META:) that arrive after a trailing '}' and ignores them for strict parse. I tried it in canary: parse_fail dropped to 0.35%.

marco: for safety, record a "repair_applied" flag in eval telemetry and add a semantic-equality check vs previous gold outputs, so we don't silently alter intent.

pat: rollout plan: 1) enable sanitizer in canary (int4 streaming only) tonight, 2) enable chunk-seq debug logging, 3) run 48h and require repaired<=0.5% and false_repair_rate<0.05% before wider rollout.

neha: filed LOG-935 (revert), RUNTIME-468 (chunk-seq), EVAL-1402 (repaired-metric).

kevin: good. if sanitizer behaves we'll add SDK opt-out flag. ping when metrics are in.

pat: will post 12h snapshot here. end.
